findings.title: Additional worker mounts need explicit dependency declarations
findings.observed: Changing an extra mounted directory changes its content hash while preserving the capture identity when it is absent from plan.dependencies and absolute check argv. A shell command with an embedded path or PYTHONPATH can consume it. Mount provenance records path/access mode only.
findings.disposition: BUILDING.md explicitly requires external check inputs in plan.dependencies. This proof uses an undeclared input, so it does not establish a defect for a conforming plan. It does establish that automatic full mounted-byte coverage is not provided by --worker-mount alone. Require all extra worker input mounts to be listed in plan.dependencies for stage4; optionally make that association automatic in a later source repair if automatic coverage is intended.
findings.root_disposition: Accepted as the documented input-declaration contract. Stage4 must list each consumed --worker-mount path in plan.dependencies. Do not claim automatic coverage of every mounted file. No source repair is required for a conforming plan.

findings.title: Python package bytes are omitted when distribution metadata has no file manifest
findings.observed: In the actual pinned worker image, importlib.metadata.distribution("pillow").files is None and file count is zero. runtime() uses dist.files or [], hashes an empty mapping and records SHA-256 44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a. Root ran the saved proof in a disposable container: changing /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/PIL/__init__.py from dd9f25c2ad1d6a7444ed64056716bbbccbdf4a3bff0b8f90ef7154aff807b786 to a different hash left the complete runtime result unchanged.
findings.impact: Before/after capture can issue a DEV CHECKED record while installed Pillow bytes differ. The unchanged image ID identifies the initial image, but does not identify changed bytes in the writable container layer. This violates the explicit worker Python-byte coverage requirement.
findings.origin: The file-manifest algorithm predates this refactor, but is exercised by the selected worker image and remains in the checked candidate.
findings.disposition: Do not advance to stage4. Launch one fresh repair stage2 to hash actual installed package bytes when metadata has no manifest or refuse an incomplete capture. Then require fresh stage3 for affected byte coverage and runtime compatibility. Reuse unrelated valid checks.

limits: This investigation reviewed source and used focused identity/environment probes. It did not duplicate the test agent fixtures.
No real target firmware/controller build, artifact equality, end-to-end speed, gate, install or device check ran here.

Mutable worker filesystem outside captured runtime dependencies is not exhaustively hashed. Normal synchronous plans must declare external inputs and avoid system mutation. Image identity alone is not an assertion that arbitrary privileged plan commands cannot alter the container.

The before/after identity contains per-run scratch mount paths and full environment including container HOSTNAME. Separate runs can have different complete identities despite matching build bytes; baseline comparison must document those bookkeeping differences without discarding real build inputs.

The earlier package-source review PASS is superseded by I2 and the actual disposable-container mutation proof. The font header equality remains valid as scoped evidence, but does not repair package provenance.
